memory_lifecycle.finding: F2-WP-300 generation 1 already implements explicit ACTIVE/DEGRADED/SUPERSEDED lifecycle transitions; payload_ref, payload_sha256 and source provenance are preserved; DELETE is not a supported transition; no clock, inferred decay, retrieval ranking or UnifiedDB persistence is claimed.

memory_lifecycle_test.finding: Source-level tests explicitly assert degradation preserves payload/provenance, supersession is redirect-only/terminal, DELETE is unsupported, stale generation/digest fail closed, and serialized contracts contain no clock/retrieval/effect/completion authority. Test-file existence is not promoted to CI/runtime credit here.

emergent_retrieval.finding: F2-WP-301 deterministically ranks explicit evidence-bound multi-axis signals and preserves RETRIEVAL_SCORE != TRUTH. It is persistence-agnostic and does not mutate lifecycle state.

emergent_retrieval_test.finding: A DEGRADED memory remains selectable and returns its preserved payload when caller-supplied scores are high. Therefore DEGRADED status by itself currently does not lower retrieval rank. SUPERSEDED memory is redirect-only and payload-suppressed.

typed_memory.finding: F2-WP-303 binds FACT/EPISODE/METHOD/PROCESS type declarations to exact WP300 lifecycle identity while explicitly denying that caller type claims mint truth. This is compatible with a salience projection that never rewrites type or source evidence.

familiarity_prediction.finding: F2-WP-302 generation 2 derives familiarity_bp from selected WP301 weighted retrieval scores and attention_priority_bp from max(familiarity, prediction_error). It validates derived WP301 scores and does not implement temporal/use-based memory decay.

wp302_falsifier_test.finding: Forged WP301 weighted/bottleneck/overlap scores are rejected before WP302 binding; this makes a new decay mechanism best expressed upstream as explicit evidence-bound WP301 axis signals, not as hidden WP302 score mutation.

aggregate_state_contradiction.observation: Phase-3 WP300-WP306 remain aggregate NOT_STARTED while granular Phase-3 source and tests are present on current main.
aggregate_state_contradiction.credit_rule: Granular source presence outranks stale aggregate for existence, but source/test-file presence alone still does not mint CI, runtime, physical-host or whole-system acceptance.

already_satisfied: immutable payload identity across lifecycle transitions
supersession rather than silent historical rewrite
retrieval as a candidate/reference plane rather than truth authority
e1_to_f2_fusion.remaining_gap: There is no deterministic evidence-bound policy that turns explicit age/verified-use/lifecycle evidence into TEMPORAL/STATE salience inputs. DEGRADED is currently a lifecycle label, not a retrieval penalty. WP301 expects caller-supplied scores; WP302 consumes WP301 output and therefore does not close this gap.
e1_to_f2_fusion.non_gap: Physical archival/deletion is a separate retention/effect-policy question and should not be conflated with ordinary retrieval forgetting.

candidate_boundary.preferred_location: WP300-derived rebuildable MemorySalienceProjection feeding WP301 TEMPORAL/STATE RetrievalSignal inputs
must_bind: explicit reference time or logical tick supplied by an authorized caller
last verified-use evidence identity if used
must_not_do: increase strength merely because the memory was retrieved
silently mutate WP301 derived rank scores after plan construction

hypothesis: A thin deterministic WP300 salience projection can close the decay gap without changing WP300 canonical lifecycle or WP301 ranking semantics: it should emit evidence-bound TEMPORAL/STATE signals that WP301 already knows how to combine.
counterhypothesis: The explicit lifecycle state alone is sufficient; callers should choose arbitrary temporal/state scores and no shared decay policy is needed.
next_discriminator: E4 deterministic ablation: hold semantic/goal/causal evidence constant and compare ACTIVE vs DEGRADED memories under (A) current caller-neutral scoring, (B) deterministic lifecycle/time salience projection, and (C) naive retrieval-count reinforcement. Measure ranking change and self-reinforcement behavior without deleting payloads.
